extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark for expert AGI. It contains 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across six disciplines, with heterogeneous image types and interleaved text-image inputs.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually curated in three stages: the authors first selected 30 subjects from six disciplines based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs; then over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary; finally, the authors cleaned duplicates, checked format/typos, and assigned difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of overly easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of the problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark questions were manually collected by over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to avoid questions with immediately available answers. Data quality control included duplicate detection via lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review of suspected duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and categorization of problems into difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed through duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, manual review by authors, format and typo checking, and difficulty categorization. The paper also reports error analysis on 150 GPT-4V error cases, with annotated error categories such as perceptual error, lack of knowledge, reasoning error, annotation error, rejection to answer, and answer extraction error.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors; additionally, 90 college senior students were used as human experts for validation, representing 30 subjects (3 per subject).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and GPT-4V shows a bias towards certain perceptual interpretations in error analysis.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature: the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI, and its design balances complexity and practicality using multiple-choice plus concise open-ended questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is positioned as a step toward evaluating Expert AGI and assessing capabilities across professional domains, with implications for how skilled adult-level performance is measured.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: A benchmark for evaluating LMMs/Expert AGI across basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities in professional domains; intended for assessment rather than training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data Quality Control: duplicate problems were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed and eliminated; problems were checked for format and typos and corrected to a standardized format; approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
